about: Delivery directions for chapter 2's voices (eleven_v4 audio tags). 'default' is per speaker; 'say' is a line's full spoken text with tags, which must equal the page text once the tags are removed. tools/directions.py checks that and writes voices.json.

say.p1-open: [wry] St Aldhelm's, a Tuesday in October, twenty past seven. [short pause] Three months after the Marrow Show, the interim vicar has talked you into learning to ring the bells.
say.p1a-2: [dry] The bicycle rack by the lychgate is empty. Hugh Daventry rings the treble, edits the parish magazine and sets the Wednesday quiz at the Plough. He usually leaves his bicycle there by a quarter past.
say.p1b-1: [pleased] Sergeant Adeyemi. You came. I told Margaret forty per cent.
say.p1b-3: [amused] She said you'd come if you'd said you would.
say.p1c-1: [too loud, brisk] You're the policeman. I'm Win. Tower captain.
say.p1c-3: [loud, stern] You sit on the bench with your feet in, and you don't touch a rope. A bell can lift a grown man to the ceiling.
say.p1d-3: [loud, brisk] Ten rows and you're back in rounds. Hugh rings the treble. If he isn't here by half past, we ring on five.
say.p2a-1: [quiet] Margaret Pike pours tea from a flask on the windowsill. She puts out two cups, looks at the second one, [short pause] and puts it back in the basket.
say.p2b-3: [loud, warning] Don't change the board, love. Hugh likes to rub it out himself.
say.p2c-1: [loud, ringing call] Look to. Treble's going. [short pause] She's gone.
say.p2d-1: [low] At a quarter past eight, the lights go out.
say.p2d-2: [low, tense] The ringing goes on in the dark, and goes wrong: a bell is missing from the pattern, or two are. Below you, through the floor, there is a thud and a short metal rattle.
say.p2d-4: [breezy, a little out of breath] That switch does it every winter. You have to hold it up.
say.p3-open: [quiet, grave] Hugh Daventry is at the foot of the tower stair, where it comes down into the vestry. Dr Achebe is kneeling beside him. [short pause] She looks up and shakes her head.
say.p3a-4: [quiet, steady] I came down for the kettle and he was here. I haven't moved him.
say.p3c-2: [weary] I was in the bath, Sam. [short pause] Tell me it's an accident.
say.p3c-4: [sharp] Then why did you ring me and not just an ambulance?
say.p4e-2: [loud, pointed] I read it when I got home. Phones stay in coats in my tower.
say.p5b-1: [smooth, sorrowful] Sergeant. Inspector. I heard this morning. Hugh and I didn't always agree, but he was good company on quiz nights.
say.p5c-1: [smooth, confident] On the five, ringing, every blow, start to finish. Five is my bell. Ask anyone in the band.
say.p5e-3: [smooth, quickly] A commission. Another church. [short pause] I'm not at liberty.
say.p6b-1: [into a microphone, cheerful] Round two. Question seven. [short pause] In what year did Monotype release the typeface Gill Sans?
say.p6b-3: [quiet, thoughtful] He was going to ask the whole village. Then tell them the answer in print.
say.p7b-1: [bright, salesman] Sergeant! Come to buy a schoolhouse? Four bedrooms, original features, a bell nobody's allowed to ring.
say.p7d-4: [hopeful] Can I still use the bit before eight?
say.p8b-2: [fond, dry] My father had a railway timetable in those letters. He kept it in the downstairs toilet.
say.p8b-5: [mild] Mr Cole told us he had regilded them.
say.p8c-1: [calm, amused] On base rates, Inspector, it is usually the person who found him. That's me. [short pause] I'd put myself at eleven per cent.
say.p8c-3: [calm] They were all in the dark with me. I can't give odds on people I couldn't see.
say.p8e-3: [mild] It was here when I unlocked this morning. I thought one of the band had brought it up.
say.p9d-4: [quick, pleased] Take the four out. 4 2 5 1 3 becomes 2 5 1 3, and by note that's 2 4 1 3. Then 4 2 3 1. Then 4 3 2 1. [short pause] Every row.
say.p10h-1: [low, fast] He was going to print it in the November magazine. Every house in the village gets one.
say.p10h-2: [quiet, flat] I went down to ask him for the page. He held on to it and stepped back, and there isn't a step there.
say.p10h-3: [quiet] And then you went back up and rang.
say.p10i-4: [quiet] The ropes come to rest. Win puts her hand flat on the wall, then looks up at the tenor's rope, still tied to its hook.
say.p10h-4: [very quiet] I didn't know what else to do.
say.p8d-3: [amused] She told me. She's bought a second chair.
say.p10f-win: [loud, indignant] I had the three, Sergeant. I kept it going in the dark. Ask Glenys.
